presets.name: 🏛️ TCJA Full Extension (CBO: $4.6T)
presets.description: Extend all TCJA individual provisions beyond 2025 sunset. Includes rate cuts, doubled standard deduction, SALT cap, pass-through deduction, CTC expansion.

presets.name: 🏛️ TCJA Extension (No SALT Cap)
presets.description: Extend TCJA but repeal the \$10K SALT cap (adds ~\$1.9T to cost). Popular bipartisan proposal.

presets.name: 🏛️ TCJA Rates Only
presets.description: Extend only the individual rate bracket cuts, not other TCJA provisions. CRS R48286 Table 1, "Reduced Individual Tax Rates": \$2,159B over FY2025-2034.

presets.name: 🏢 Biden Corporate 28% (CBO: -$1.35T)
presets.description: Raise corporate rate from 21% to 28%. CBO estimate: raises ~\$1.35T over 10 years.

presets.name: 🏢 Trump Corporate 15%
presets.description: Lower corporate rate from 21% to 15%, with bonus depreciation extended. Published estimates of the rate change alone run \$595B (PWBM) to \$673B (Tax Foundation) over ten years.

presets.name: 👶 Biden CTC Expansion (CBO: $1.6T)
presets.description: Expand CTC to \$3,600/\$3,000 per child, fully refundable. Based on 2021 ARP expansion.

presets.name: 👶 CTC Extension (CBO: $600B)
presets.description: Extend current \$2,000 CTC beyond 2025 sunset. Without extension, reverts to \$1,000.

presets.name: 💼 EITC Childless Expansion (Treasury: $163B)
presets.description: Triple EITC for childless workers (~\$1,500 max), expand age range to 19-65+.

presets.name: 🏠 Estate Tax: Extend TCJA (CBO: $167B)
presets.description: Keep ~\$14M exemption (vs \$6.4M if TCJA expires). Costs ~\$167B over 10 years.

presets.name: 🏠 Biden Estate Reform (-$450B)
presets.description: Lower exemption to \$3.5M, raise rate to 45%. Raises ~\$450B over 10 years.

presets.name: 🏠 Eliminate Estate Tax ($407B)
presets.description: Repeal federal estate tax entirely. Tax Foundation's *Options 3.0* Option 83 puts it at \$407B over CY2027-2036 -- a row that repeals the estate **and gift** taxes, so it is the broader of the two.

presets.name: 💰 SS Cap to 90% (CBO: -$800B)
presets.description: Raise Social Security cap to cover 90% of wages (~\$305K). Raises ~\$800B.

presets.name: 💰 SS Donut Hole $250K (-$1.43T)
presets.description: Apply SS tax to wages above \$250K (donut hole). CBO's *Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2025 to 2034* Option 62 alternative 2 scores the same design at \$1,427B over FY2025-2034. The model still returns \$2,700B, because its covered-wage band was set from the superseded target and retuning it would hide the miss.

presets.name: 💰 Eliminate SS Cap (-$3.2T)
presets.description: Eliminate Social Security wage cap entirely. Raises ~\$3.2T over 10 years.

presets.name: 💰 Expand NIIT (JCT: -$250B)
presets.description: Apply 3.8% NIIT to S-corp/partnership income. Raises ~\$250B over 10 years.

presets.name: ⚖️ AMT: Extend TCJA Relief ($1.36T)
presets.description: Extend TCJA's higher AMT exemptions (\$88K single, \$137K MFJ) past 2025. CRS/CBO put the 10-year cost at ~\$1.36T.

presets.name: ⚖️ Repeal Individual AMT ($450B)
presets.description: Fully repeal individual AMT. After TCJA expires, would cost ~\$450B over 10 years.

presets.name: ⚖️ Repeal Corporate AMT (+$220B)
presets.description: Repeal the 15% corporate book minimum tax (CAMT) enacted by IRA 2022. **Costs** ~\$220B over 10 years: JCT scored enacting CAMT as a \$222.2B revenue raiser (JCX-18-22), so repeal loses that revenue.

presets.name: 🏥 Extend ACA Enhanced PTCs ($335B)
presets.description: Extend enhanced premium tax credits (ARPA/IRA) past 2025. Costs ~\$335B over FY2025-2034 (CBO/JCT pub. 60437).

presets.name: 🏥 Repeal ACA Premium Credits (-$1.1T)
presets.description: Repeal all ACA premium subsidies. Saves ~\$1.1T but ~19M lose subsidized coverage.

presets.name: 📋 Cap Employer Health Exclusion (-$450B)
presets.description: Cap tax exclusion for employer health insurance at \$50K. Raises ~\$450B over 10 years.

presets.name: 📋 Repeal SALT Cap ($1.17T)
presets.description: Remove the cap on the state and local tax deduction, scored against current law — P.L. 119-21 sec. 70120 sets it at \$40,400 in 2026 rising 1%/yr through 2029, phased down above \$500K of income, reverting to \$10K in 2030. Penn Wharton's ~\$1.17T prices the same repeal against a permanent \$10K cap, and ~\$197B against a baseline where the cap expires.

presets.name: 📋 Eliminate Step-Up Basis (-$500B)
presets.description: Tax capital gains at death with \$1M exemption. Raises ~\$500B over 10 years.

presets.name: 📋 Cap Charitable Deduction (-$200B)
presets.description: Limit charitable deduction value to 28% rate. Raises ~\$200B over 10 years.

presets.name: Biden 2025 Proposal
presets.description: +2.6pp on income above \$400K, restoring the pre-TCJA 39.6% top rate. Treasury FY2025 Green Book estimate: raises ~\$252B over 10 years.

presets.name: Progressive Millionaire Tax
presets.description: 5pp surtax on income above \$1M, scored on the AGI-inclusive base — capital gains and qualified dividends included. **No official score**: nothing published scores this reform, so the model's own estimate is the only number shown, and the AGI-inclusive base is a design choice of the preset by analogy with the Warren and Medicare surtaxes rather than a reading of a source document.

presets.name: Middle Class Tax Cut
presets.description: 2pp cut for households earning \$50K+

presets.name: Flat Tax Reform
presets.description: Lower all rates by 5pp (illustrative)

presets.name: Warren Ultra-Millionaire Surtax
presets.description: 3pp surtax on **AGI** above \$2M, Warren-style, scored on the AGI-inclusive base its TPC source uses — realized capital gains and qualified dividends included. Raises roughly \$300-400B over 10 years depending on behavioral response.

presets.name: Top Rate to 45%
presets.description: Raise the top marginal rate from 37% to 45% on income above the current 37% bracket floor (\$609,350 single, 2025). Illustrative of the upper end of progressive proposals. **No official score**: the \$420B figure this preset used to quote could not be traced to any TPC, CBO or JCT publication and was withdrawn in the Phase E provenance pass, so the model's own estimate is the only number shown.

presets.name: High-Earner Medicare Surcharge 2pp
presets.description: +2pp Medicare surcharge on wage **and investment** income above \$400K, scored on the AGI-inclusive base Treasury's FY2025 Green Book row uses. Extends the NIIT's 3.8% surtax logic to a broader base. Similar in structure to the Biden 2025 Medicare surtax proposal.

presets.name: 🌍 Biden GILTI Reform (-$374B)
presets.description: Country-by-country GILTI at 21%, eliminate QBAI exemption. Raises ~\$374B over 10 years (Treasury FY2025 Green Book).

presets.name: 🌍 Repeal FDII (-$158B)
presets.description: Repeal Foreign-Derived Intangible Income deduction. Raises ~\$158B over 10 years (Treasury FY2025 Green Book, before the R&D proposal Treasury pairs it with).

presets.name: 🌍 Pillar Two Adoption (-$80B)
presets.description: Adopt OECD Pillar Two 15% global minimum tax. JCT estimate: raises ~\$80B.

presets.name: 🌍 Biden International Package (-$632B)
presets.description: Full Biden international reform: GILTI at 21% per-country + FDII repeal + UTPR. Raises ~\$632B (Treasury FY2025 Green Book subtotal).

presets.name: 🔍 IRA Enforcement Funding (-$180B)
presets.description: IRA IRS enforcement funding. CBO: raises ~\$180B of revenue over FY2022-2031 (pub. 58390), about \$101B net of the \$79B appropriation.

presets.name: 🔍 Double IRS Enforcement (-$340B)
presets.description: Double IRS enforcement beyond IRA levels (~\$16B/year). Raises ~\$340B with diminishing returns. **Illustrative**: an unfitted reconstruction a long way from its published figure, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 🔍 High-Income Enforcement
presets.description: Targeted enforcement for >\$400K returns and large partnerships. \$5B/year, high ROI. **No official score**: nothing published scores a *targeted* high-income enforcement increase. CBO scores *untargeted* appropriations only — \$20B of funding for −\$41B of deficit and \$40B for −\$63B (publication 59972, FY2024-2034). The model's own estimate is the only number shown.

presets.name: 💊 Expand Drug Negotiation (-$500B)
presets.description: Negotiate 50 Medicare drugs (vs IRA's 20), remove exclusivity delays. Saves ~\$500B. **Illustrative**: an unfitted reconstruction a long way from its published figure, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 💊 Universal Insulin Cap ($11B)
presets.description: \$35/month insulin cap for Medicare and private insurance. A cost-sharing cap shifts liability onto plans, so CBO scores it as adding ~\$11B to the deficit over 10 years. **Illustrative**: an unfitted reconstruction a long way from its published figure, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 💊 International Reference Pricing (-$100B)
presets.description: Cap Medicare drug prices at 120% of OECD international average. Saves ~\$100B. **Illustrative**: an unfitted reconstruction a long way from its published figure, shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 💊 Comprehensive Drug Reform
presets.description: Expanded negotiation + insulin cap + manufacturer discounts. **No official score**: nothing published scores a *combined* package of these three, and the nearest published figures are components an order of magnitude smaller (CBO put the IRA's own negotiation at \$98.5B over FY2022-2031). The model's own estimate is the only number shown, and it is a 🟡 reconstruction of a channel nobody has scored. **Illustrative**: shown for the shape of the policy rather than as an estimate of it.

presets.name: 🏭 Trump Universal 10% Tariff (-$2.17T)
presets.description: 10% tariff on all imports. Raises ~\$2.17T conventionally (Tax Foundation FF861) but costs ~\$1,700/household in higher prices.

presets.name: 🏭 Trump 60% China Tariff (-$650B)
presets.description: 60% tariff on all Chinese imports (~\$430B base). CRFB's *Options to Raise Tariff Revenue* scores it at \$650B over FY2026-2035, and notes savings would run about 15% lower on FY2025-2034.

presets.name: 🏭 25% Auto Tariff (-$386B)
presets.description: 25% tariff on imported vehicles and parts (~\$380B base). Raises ~\$386B conventionally (Tax Foundation tariff tracker).

presets.name: 🏭 25% Steel/Aluminum Tariff (-$60B)
presets.description: 25% tariff on steel and aluminum imports (~\$50B base).

presets.name: 🏭 Reciprocal Tariffs (-$1.5T)
presets.description: Match trading partners' tariff rates (~20pp average increase). Published conventional estimates of the announced schedule span \$1.4-1.8T; the official score shown anchors on Tax Foundation's \$1.5T.
presets.cbo_source: CRFB / Tax Foundation / Yale Budget Lab

presets.name: 🌱 Repeal IRA Clean Energy Credits (-$851B)
presets.description: Full repeal of IRA clean energy tax credits. Tax Foundation (McBride, House Oversight testimony, May 2025) puts it at \$851B over FY2025-2034. The \$783B this used to cite to a March 2024 CBO publication was the model's own output: no CBO or JCT document carries it.

presets.name: 🌱 Carbon Tax \$50/ton (-$1.7T)
presets.description: \$50/ton CO2 tax with 5% annual escalator. Raises ~\$1.7T over 10 years.

presets.name: 🌱 Carbon Tax \$25/ton
presets.description: \$25/ton CO2 starter tax with 5% annual escalator. **No official score is quoted**: a real document does exist, on a different decade — CBO and JCT's *Options for Reducing the Deficit: 2023 to 2032* scores \$25/tonne rising 5% plus inflation at −\$865B over FY2023-2032 — but this repository has no scorecard row for it, so the model's own estimate is the only number shown.

presets.name: 🌱 Repeal EV Credits (-$182B)
presets.description: Repeal the \$7,500 clean-vehicle credit (sec. 30D) and the commercial clean-vehicle credit (sec. 45W). Saves ~\$182B over FY2025-2034 (JCT JCX-35-25).

presets.name: 🌱 Extend IRA Credits Beyond 2032
presets.description: Extend IRA clean energy credits 5 years beyond the 2032 sunset. **No official score**: every published figure scores the credits *as enacted* or their *repeal*, never an incremental five-year extension. The model's own estimate is the only number shown.
